hypothesis: A bounded population with explicit recombination and an unbounded counter-based task stream can sustain evolutionary attempts across extinction episodes; useful predictive capability is not expected or guaranteed.
goal: Global aspiration: strive toward error-free prediction of unknown computational processes; this is not a finite falsifiable success claim.

population.selection: noisy tournament on current task accuracy
population.replacement: lowest current score; stochastic survival permits regressions

recombination: single-point component crossover of modules, router, search, dialect and memory; offspring is validated by fixed external ABI
task_arrivals: counter-based SHA-256 seed derivation per task index; deterministic infinite index stream over registered task families; expanding families requires a new protocol version
extinction: when no active individuals remain, emit recolonization event and start a distinct episode from the preserved bounded diversity archive; registered ancestor is fallback only if archive is empty; never claim lineage continuity
evolutionary_changes: inheritable search bytecode, predictor modules, routing, dialect semantics, memory and module composition remain mutable under existing VM limits
external_invariants: VM ABI and hard instruction/fuel limits

resource_caps.archive_policy: stop at a cap; segment via explicit registered archival procedure; no silent pruning

measurement: Record each candidate, parent IDs, mutation and recombination, score, task family/index/seed, cost, acceptance and extinctions. Search continuity is not scientific progress. Report capability separately from infrastructure uptime and attempt counts.
limits: No multi-year soak or Linux production acceptance
No task-family growth beyond the registered deterministic stream
One active experimental implementation may still need external supervisor integration
